issues.legal_issue: Identification of an accused not named in the initial report can be reliable when the report says the witnesses can identify the assailants and a witness names the accused to police promptly.
material_facts: The initial report did not name the alleged shooters but stated that the informant could identify them.
A witness who was at the scene named the accused to police on the day of the incident, and the names were recorded in the investigation materials made that day.
The informant’s account was corroborated in material respects, and the accused declined to participate in an identification parade.
issues.conclusion: The identification evidence was reliable and supported the accused’s conviction.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the identification evidence in the context of the prompt naming, the witnesses’ presence and accounts, and the other evidence. It cited no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this evidentiary assessment; the conviction under appeal included one under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and eyewitness_present_at_scene and witness_named_accused_promptly and (informant_reserved_ability_to_identify or accused_declined_identification_parade) and witness_accounts_corroborated

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.eyewitness_present_at_scene: A witness who observed the incident was present at the scene.
predicates.witness_named_accused_promptly: A witness identified the accused to investigators promptly after the incident.
predicates.informant_reserved_ability_to_identify: The initial report stated that the informant could identify the assailants despite not naming them.
predicates.accused_declined_identification_parade: The accused declined to participate in an identification parade.
predicates.witness_accounts_corroborated: The witnesses’ accounts were corroborated in material respects by other evidence.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns a conviction and the stated eyewitness and corroboration facts are present, the identification evidence supports the conviction.

issues.legal_issue: The evidentiary value of an extra-judicial confession depends on the circumstances in which it was made, its timing, and the credibility of the witness who recounts it.
material_facts: The accused and others made statements admitting involvement in the killing to a cooperative society official who had known them for several years.
The official had been approached because of his perceived influence with police and had previously been involved in a dispute between the parties.
The official had no established personal interest in the matter, testified to the statements, and was also a witness to the weapon recoveries.
issues.conclusion: The confession evidence was credible in the circumstances and could be relied on.
issues.legal_principle: The court stated that an extra-judicial confession must be assessed in the factual situation of each case, including the nature of the circumstances, the time of the confession, and the credibility of the witness. It cited no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this principle.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and accused_made_extra_judicial_confession and confession_witness_was_credible and confession_had_plausible_context

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.accused_made_extra_judicial_confession: The accused made a confession outside a formal court proceeding.
predicates.confession_witness_was_credible: The person recounting the confession was found credible and had no established personal interest in the case.
predicates.confession_had_plausible_context: The circumstances provided a plausible reason for the accused to make the confession to that person.

issues.definition: When an accused makes an extra-judicial confession to a credible witness in a plausible context, the confession may be relied on in deciding the criminal appeal.

issues.legal_issue: An inconclusive forensic comparison of recovered weapons and crime-scene cartridges does not by itself negate guilt when other evidence supports the conviction.
material_facts: Weapons were recovered following information supplied by the accused and another person.
The forensic examination could not determine whether the crime-scene cartridges had been fired from those weapons because there were insufficient identifying marks.
The prosecution also relied on eyewitness evidence, confession evidence, and evidence of motive.
issues.conclusion: The inconclusive forensic result did not establish that the accused had not committed the crime and did not undermine the conviction.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that the inability to match the recovered weapons conclusively to the cartridges, by itself, did not lead to the conclusion that the accused had not committed the crime. It cited no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this evidentiary conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and weapon_recovered_after_accused_information and forensic_comparison_inconclusive and other_evidence_supports_guilt

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.weapon_recovered_after_accused_informati: A weapon was recovered after the accused supplied information leading to its recovery.
predicates.forensic_comparison_inconclusive: Forensic examination could not determine whether the weapon fired the crime-scene ammunition.
predicates.other_evidence_supports_guilt: Evidence apart from the forensic comparison supports the accused’s guilt.

issues.definition: When a weapon is recovered after the accused’s information, the forensic comparison is inconclusive, and other evidence supports guilt, the inconclusive result does not negate guilt.

issues.legal_issue: Proof that payment was made to a person alleged to have been hired to commit a killing is not necessary where the court finds the other evidence of guilt sufficient.
material_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused had been hired to kill the deceased.
The court found evidence identifying the accused as an assailant and relied on confession evidence and evidence of the dispute and motive.
The prosecution did not prove that money had passed to the accused.
issues.conclusion: The absence of proof that payment was made did not prevent the court from sustaining the conviction.
issues.legal_principle: The court stated that proof of payment to the accused was not necessary and observed that the matter was within the accused persons’ special knowledge. It cited no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and hired_killing_alleged and other_evidence_supports_guilt and payment_not_proved

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.hired_killing_alleged: The prosecution alleged that the accused was hired to commit the killing.
predicates.other_evidence_supports_guilt: Evidence apart from proof of payment supports the accused’s guilt.
predicates.payment_not_proved: The prosecution did not establish that payment was made to the accused.

issues.definition: When a hired killing is alleged, other evidence supports guilt, and payment is unproved, proof of payment is not required to sustain the conviction.
